topic: Cyril Radcliffe drew the India-Pakistan border in five weeks having never visited India, then vanished before it was published
title: The Man Who Drew India And Pakistan's Border In 5 Weeks
description: AI-narrated commentary: the British lawyer who drew the India-Pakistan border in five weeks without ever having visited India, then left before it was even published.

hook_candidates.text: The total stranger behind India and Pakistan's border, drawn in five weeks flat.
What if the line between India and Pakistan had been drawn by someone who'd never set foot in either country?
You'd assume a border cutting through a billion people took decades of expert planning. This one took five weeks.
In July 1947, a British lawyer received a blank map of India and exactly five weeks.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks every national border was drawn by regional experts after years of careful negotiation, because they want to prove one was drawn by a total stranger in five weeks.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a border as significant as India and Pakistan's was drawn by regional experts over years, but it was drawn by an outsider in five weeks.
closing_comment: The wildest part is the man who drew this border refused his fee and vanished before it was even published, so what would you have done with only five weeks?

sources.note: Confirms Radcliffe had never visited India, was given five weeks, and the line split canals, railways, and villages.
Confirms Radcliffe refused his fee, burned his papers, left before the line published, and his 'eighty million' quote.

beats.text: British officials picked him specifically because he had **never** been to India.

beats.text: They believed total unfamiliarity would look more **impartial** than any actual regional expert's judgment.

a fake diploma certificate reading Total Unfamiliarity in an ornate gold frame, comedic still life

beats.text: He drew the whole line from outdated maps, never visiting **one village** it touched.
beats.broll_query: a dusty stack of old paper maps and census ledgers on a wooden desk, single lamp, no people

beats.text: The line sliced through **canals**, railways, and farms that had shared water for generations.

a red and white border post planted crookedly in a farmyard beside a bewildered barn, illustration style

beats.text: He wrote that **eighty million** people with a grievance would soon be looking for him.

beats.text: He left India the day before independence, then **burned** every note he'd made.

beats.text: Historians still **debate** whether any expert could have prevented what followed.
